record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Possible separation between existence and continuous minimization
record.original_question: In the degree-zero harmonic-map setting from B^3 to S^2, can it happen that no minimizer exists for the energy infimum over continuous competitors, yet a continuous harmonic map with the prescribed boundary data still exists?

evidence.quote: Clearly, a positive answer to Open Problem 4.2 would provide a solution to Open Problem 4.1. But in principle it might happen that the answer to Open Problem 4.2 is negative while the answer to Problem 4.1 is positive. (Can this scenario occcur?)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3$ denote the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and $S^2$ the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$. For a map $u\in H^1(B^3;S^2)$ the Dirichlet energy is
$$E(u)=\int_{B^3}|\nabla u|^2\,dx.$$
Fix a smooth boundary datum $g:\partial B^3\to S^2$ of topological degree zero, and let
$$\mathcal{C}_g=\{u\in C^0(\overline{B^3};S^2)\cap H^1(B^3;S^2):u|_{\partial B^3}=g\}.$$
Set $I(g)=\inf\{E(u):u\in\mathcal{C}_g\}$. A continuous harmonic map with boundary datum $g$ is a map $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ that is weakly harmonic (i.e.\ $-\Delta u=u|\nabla u|^2$ in the sense of distributions).

Question: Does there exist a smooth boundary datum $g:\partial B^3\to S^2$ of degree zero for which:
(i) the infimum $I(g)$ is not attained by any $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ (no continuous minimizer exists), yet
(ii) there nevertheless exists a continuous harmonic map $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ with $u|_{\partial B^3}=g$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems and is connected to a long-standing question of R. Schoen on the existence of continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 with prescribed boundary data. No resolution appears in available sources; the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems — Haïm Brezis
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 4.1 (Schoen) and 4.2 concerning continuous harmonic maps and minimizers from B^3 to S^2 with degree-zero boundary data; explicit remark that the scenario where 4.2 fails but 4.1 holds is not excluded.
status_evidence.claim: Brezis lists these as open problems and explicitly asks whether the described separation can occur.

status_evidence.title: Some of my favorite open problems (EMS)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems including those on harmonic maps from the 3-ball to the 2-sphere.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as open in this published collection.
